title: Surface-informed active learning selects a tested Ni55Co10Fe35 oxygen-evolution catalyst
summary: Researchers used Gaussian-process active learning with DFT adsorption energies to select a nickel–cobalt–iron alloy precursor. Synthesized Ni55Co10Fe35 required 327 mV overpotential at 10 mA/cm² in alkaline laboratory tests, versus 380 mV for NiFe and 404 mV for CoFe controls. Its Tafel slope was 43.07 mV/decade. Prediction and experimental activity maps did not fully agree; this supports compositional narrowing, not quantitative performance prediction. The working surface reconstructs into oxyhydroxides, which the alloy-surface model does not represent.
organization: Kyonggi University; Seoul National University; Dongguk University; Korea University

evidence.tested: Synthesized alloy tested by rotating-disk electrochemistry in 1 M KOH; approximately 24-hour stability test.
evidence.unknown: Broader material-system generalization remains prospective. Supplement and raw data not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: GPR learned adsorption-energy relationships and selected further DFT configurations, narrowing the alloy composition for experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Publisher full text, including Results and Discussion and main Methods; supporting information and raw datasets not reviewed.
